item.title: Solved: How to Implement Digit Recognition OCR in OpenCV-Python
item.description:
Overview

Creating a Digit Recognition OCR system using OpenCV and Python is an excellent project for both learning and practical application. In this guide, we will explore the KNearest and SVM algorithms to achieve digit recognition with a dataset of 100 samples for each digit. We will begin by understanding how to prepare the data, train the model, and test the digit recognition using OpenCV’s capabilities.

What is the letter_recognition.data file?

The letter_recognition.data file serves as a training dataset that allows the model to learn and differentiate between various digits based on sample images. This file is crucial for both KNearest and SVM algorithms, as it contains the necessary features and corresponding labels for classification.

item.title: Top 5 Methods to Install Python OpenCV through Anaconda
item.description:
When it comes to installing OpenCV for Python through Anaconda, many users face various challenges and hurdles. If you have tried executing commands like:

or

item.title: Solved: How to Generate a Depth Map from Uncalibrated Stereo System Using OpenCV
item.description:
I’m currently working on generating a depth map using uncalibrated stereo images and want to share my approach and seek guidance on improving my results.

Here’s the process I followed to obtain the depth map:

  1. Feature Detection Using SIFT:
    I started by utilizing the Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) to identify corresponding points in the stereo image pair. The implementation is shown in the code snippet below:

    import cv2 as cv
import numpy as np

# Initialize SIFT detector
sift = cv.SIFT_create()

# Detect and compute keypoints and descriptors
kp1, des1 = sift.detectAndCompute(dst1, None)
kp2, des2 = sift.detectAndCompute(dst2, None)

# Parameters for FLANN matcher
FLANN_INDEX_KDTREE = 0
index_params = dict(algorithm=FLANN_INDEX_KDTREE, trees=5)
search_params = dict(checks=50)

flann = cv.FlannBasedMatcher(index_params, search_params)
matches = flann.knnMatch(des1, des2, k=2)

good = []
pts1 = []
pts2 = []

# Lowe's ratio test
for i, (m, n) in enumerate(matches):
    if m.distance < 0.8 * n.distance:
        good.append(m)
        pts2.append(kp2[m.trainIdx].pt)
        pts1.append(kp1[m.queryIdx].pt)

pts1 = np.array(pts1)
pts2 = np.array(pts2)
